How memory cell layouts evolve

Memory cells combine a transistor and a capacitor, which complicates scaling. Changing the layout requires careful engineering.

Cell geometry describes the layout, while the process node determines the size of its components.


Competitors are exploring smaller footprints, but manufacturing costs also matter.

Capacitor spacing can limit density even when transistors become smaller.


Manufacturers can improve established layouts with new materials and wafer bonding.

Vertical memory stacks require changes to the architecture and thermal design.

Further research will determine when these designs become practical.
